correctness.rationale: The square ideal W=V tensor V is invariant under derivations by Leibniz on products, and annihilates the algebra. Therefore the V-to-V block A and arbitrary shear F determine the W action rho(A), and conversely these maps satisfy Leibniz. Injectivity of rho follows by applying it to e_i tensor e_i, reading off the off-diagonals and then dividing the diagonal coefficient by two. Locality keeps W invariant. For its W-block C, the tested image of u tensor v lies in V tensor v + u tensor V. Coefficients of e_i tensor (e_j+e_l) imply the first-factor off-diagonal coefficients are independent of the second index, and the transposed comparison does the same for the second factor. After subtracting these tensor-sum actions, the four-entry test on (e_i+e_h) tensor (e_j+e_l) forces additive diagonal coefficients d_ij=alpha_i+beta_j. Thus C=A_0 tensor I + I tensor B_0; flip symmetry on u tensor u forces (A_0-B_0)u proportional to u for every u, hence scalar by basis sums. Division by two gives the unique common parameter S. At nonzero v an arbitrary shear can prescribe its value at v and correct any difference on z, so A and S are truly independent for one-point locality. The two-point argument is valid because D^{-1}(T-S) is skew-symmetric when (T-S)D+D(T-S)^T=0, and e_i and e_i+e_j with diagonal signs 1 and -1 eliminate every mismatch entry over any field of characteristic not two. A shorter independent check of the same rigidity uses the pair v,v^2: the shared derivation enforces rho(S-A)(v tensor v)=0. Testing v=e_i forces (S-A)e_i=0 from the off-diagonal tensor coefficients and twice the diagonal coefficient. Counting free blocks gives the stated dimensions and defect. These arguments do not require an infinite field or a rank beyond the stated m>=2.
residual_risks: The replay is not an arbitrary-field proof or a full reflexive-hull enumeration; those general quantifiers follow from the coefficient argument. Characteristic two, quotients and nonlinear two-local maps are not assessed.

evidence: The null-filiform paper's Theorem 5.5 even treats nonlinear two-local derivations on its null-filiform algebra, but the generator count and multiplication differ. Its filiform and naturally graded quasi-filiform families have near-maximal nilpotency lengths, unlike an m+m^2 dimensional cube-zero algebra.
The broader nilpotent Lie/right Leibniz paper works with different products over the complex field.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Stronger two-local conclusions on a different class do not subsume this one. Passing to a Lie commutator probes the alternating sector and loses the symmetric square evaluations which enforce rigidity here.

originality.rationale: The distinctive result is the pointwise evaluation hull of the ordered tensor-square action and the corresponding exact local derivation classification. The ordinary normal form is prior, and the two-local collapse is a substantive contrast with the Lie case but follows efficiently once the local classification is known (the pair v,v^2 suffices). Neither a same-algebra idempotent census nor the associative filiform classification establishes the local hull for this multiplication.

value.rationale: The cube-zero free associative algebra is a natural benchmark outside the commonly treated one-generated filiform families. The classification explains which parameters can vary independently under one-point interpolation and why that freedom disappears at two points. It gives a complete all-rank invariant, with a meaningful difference from the exterior-square Lie model, rather than a finite-field sample or an ordinary-derivation recount.
residual_risks: The claimed classification is for linear maps over fields of characteristic not two and does not resolve nonlinear two-local maps or more general quadratic truncations.
